articles.title: Silent and Costly: Characterizing and Detecting Prompt-Caching Mis-Integration in LLM Agents
articles.summary: The paper studies prompt-caching integration problems across 120 pull requests in 10 popular open-source LLM agent systems, finding that errors often occur through request-side misconfiguration or read-side usage miscount. These failures are especially costly because they typically fail silently, creating inference cost and latency leakage without obvious runtime errors. The authors introduce CACHELINT, which found additional real-world issues across 571 agent projects, producing developer confirmations and upstream fixes, including one in Anthropic's official SDK.
articles.advisor_relevance: This highlights a practical bottleneck in enterprise and agentic AI adoption: cost-saving features such as prompt caching can be difficult to implement correctly and may silently erode expected economics. For advisors, it reinforces that AI monetization depends not only on model capability but also on infrastructure efficiency, developer tooling, and operational controls around production deployments.
